analysis.overview: UNSW undergraduate course (Term 2 2026, 6 UOC) following LAWS1022/JURD7121 Crime and the Criminal Process. Applies contextual, critical perspectives to doctrinally central criminal offences and defences in NSW, stressing policy, race, class and gender, interdisciplinary materials, and legal element analysis of statutory and common law. Assessed by assignment (30%), class participation (10%) and final invigilated examination (60%).

study_notes: Assignment is a 1200-word problem scenario on sentencing; only simple editing AI assistance permitted.
Final invigilated exam contains one problem scenario and one essay question; no generative AI permitted.
Sentencing is explored via five self-paced online modules in addition to seminars.
Required textbook: Brown et al, Criminal Laws (8th ed, Federation Press, 2025); Howie and Johnson's Annotated Criminal Legislation NSW recommended.
Course follows LAWS1021/JURD7121; electronic resources cannot be accessed in invigilated exams.
